hosts.block: Don't block it. It sits behind Apple hosts such as mesu.apple.com and swcdn.apple.com, so updates and other Apple services can fail.
breaks: Apple hosts that resolve through it, such as software update hosts, may become unreachable.
Apple doesn't list every host that uses it, so other Apple services may fail too.
hosts.summary: An Apple domain behind Apple's content delivery. Many apple.com hosts resolve to names under it, so connections show up with it.

hosts.block: Don't block them. Signing in to your Apple Account in System Settings can fail.
breaks: Signing in, or managing your Apple Account, in System Settings can fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for Apple Account authentication in Settings and System Settings.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Setting up, restoring and some updates need device activation.
breaks: Setting up or restoring a Mac may fail at activation.
Installing or updating macOS may fail, since Apple lists it for those too.
hosts.summary: Apple's device activation host, needed during setup and when installing, updating or restoring the operating system.

hosts.block: Blocking them can stop links from opening in their apps, and other features built on Associated Domains.
breaks: Universal links may open in the browser instead of the app.
Other features built on Associated Domains may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for Associated Domains, which universal links and other app-to-website links rely on.

hosts.block: Don't block it. iCloud sync for many apps stops, and macOS can't do notarization checks for apps.
breaks: Apps that keep data in iCloud stop syncing between your devices.
Gatekeeper's notarization checks can't reach Apple.
Screen Time and iCloud Keychain sync stop, since Apple says that they use CloudKit.
hosts.summary: Apple's CloudKit service. Apps sync their iCloud data through it, and Apple lists api.apple-cloudkit.com for app notarization on macOS.

hosts.block: Don't block it. iCloud hosts resolve through it, so iCloud services can become unreachable.
breaks: iCloud hosts that resolve through it, such as gateway.icloud.com, may become unreachable.
hosts.summary: Apple's domain for the DNS of iCloud services. iCloud hosts resolve through names under it.

hosts.block: Blocking it may stop Apple Intelligence Extensions. Apple doesn't document which features those are.
breaks: Apple Intelligence features that use extensions may fail.
hosts.summary: The Apple host that Apple lists for Apple Intelligence Extensions.

hosts.block: Blocking it can stop App Store content from loading or downloading. Turn off automatic updates instead.
breaks: App Store pages, apps and updates may fail to load or download.
hosts.summary: Apple's store content host, for apps, books and music, next to *.itunes.apple.com.

hosts.block: Safe to block if you don't use GarageBand. If you do, its extra sounds and instruments can't download.
breaks: GarageBand's downloadable sounds and instruments can't download.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for GarageBand downloadable content.

hosts.block: Don't block it. The Mac can't tell that a hotel or café network wants a sign-in, so the sign-in window may never appear.
breaks: The sign-in window for hotel, café and airport Wi-Fi may not appear.
The Mac may treat a working network as having no internet, or the other way round.
Kilobat's Wi-Fi sign-in detection can't tell a sign-in page from an outage.
hosts.summary: Apple's internet connectivity check for networks with sign-in pages (captive portals). Kilobat uses it too.

hosts.block: Don't block the whole domain. iCloud, software updates and Apple Account sign-in use hosts under it.
breaks: iCloud services may fail.
Software update downloads from updates.cdn-apple.com fail.
Apple Account sign-in in System Settings may fail.
hosts.summary: An Apple content delivery domain. Apple lists it for iCloud services; update and sign-in hosts sit under it too.

hosts.block: Blocking it can stop Rosetta 2 from installing or updating, so Intel-only apps may not run on a Mac with Apple silicon.
breaks: Rosetta 2 updates can't download.
Intel-only apps may fail to open if Rosetta 2 isn't installed yet.
hosts.summary: The Apple host that Apple lists for Rosetta 2 updates on macOS.

hosts.block: Don't block them. The Mac can't fetch Apple's revocation lists or certificates, and Apple services can fail validation.
breaks: Revoked Apple-issued certificates may not be detected.
Certificate validation for Apple's services may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for certificate revocation lists and certificates, used to validate the certificates of Apple's services.

hosts.block: Blocking it may stop hardware diagnostics that need Apple's servers. Nothing else documented depends on it.
breaks: Diagnostics that check for hardware issues may fail to run or to finish.
hosts.summary: The Apple host that devices use for diagnostics that help detect possible hardware issues.

hosts.block: Don't block them. Apple lists them for certificate validation, and websites with DigiCert certificates need them too.
breaks: Certificate checks for Apple services that use DigiCert certificates may fail.
Revocation checks for websites with DigiCert certificates may fail.
hosts.summary: DigiCert's certificate status and revocation list hosts. Apple lists them because some of its services use DigiCert certificates.

hosts.block: Blocking it stops Chrome and other Google apps from updating, including security fixes.
breaks: Chrome updates can't download, so security fixes wait.
Other Google downloads from this host fail too.
hosts.summary: Google's download host, where Chrome gets its updates.

hosts.block: Blocking it can break the encrypted DNS lookups that macOS sends to Apple. Normal DNS through your router isn't affected.
breaks: Encrypted DNS lookups to Apple fail. Apps that depend on them may not connect.
Features that use Apple's DoH, which Apple doesn't list, may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's DNS over HTTPS (DoH) host. Apple lists it for encrypted DNS resolution in macOS Big Sur and later.

hosts.block: Safe to block if you don't use Xcode. If you do, Xcode can't download the components it needs.
breaks: Xcode can't download platform support, simulators and other components.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for Xcode's downloadable components.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops the Dropbox app and website. To save data, pause syncing in the Dropbox app instead.
breaks: The Dropbox desktop app can't sign in or sync.
dropbox.com doesn't load in the browser.
hosts.summary: Dropbox's official domains for its product, API and static content.

hosts.block: Blocking them can break Dropbox downloads, shared links and syncing. Dropbox doesn't document each host's role.
breaks: Downloads from Dropbox, including shared links, may fail.
Syncing in the desktop app may fail.
hosts.summary: A Dropbox domain on its list of verified domains, with hosts such as dl.dropboxusercontent.com.

hosts.block: Don't block it. macOS uses it for CloudKit content, and Apple says that XProtect updates come from it.
breaks: XProtect malware definitions and other CloudKit content can't download, so the Mac's malware protection falls behind.
Voice Control assets can't download.
Apple says that its services fail any connection that uses HTTPS interception, so a proxy that inspects TLS also breaks it.
hosts.summary: Apple's CloudKit gateway. Apple lists it for CloudKit content, including XProtect malware definitions and Voice Control assets.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Software Update and device management can't see which updates exist.
breaks: macOS may not find software updates.
On a managed Mac, the management service may not see or enforce updates.
Updates for additional components may not be found.
hosts.summary: Apple's software update catalog host. Device management services also ask it which updates are available.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Apple lists it for setup and for operating system updates, so updates and restores can fail.
breaks: macOS updates may fail to install.
Setting up or restoring a device may fail.
hosts.summary: An Apple host that devices need during setup and for operating system updates. Apple lists it in both sections of its host list.

hosts.block: Safe to block if you don't use Siri or server dictation. It's cleaner to turn Siri off in System Settings.
breaks: Siri requests that need Apple's servers fail.
Dictation that uses Apple's servers fails.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for Siri and dictation requests.

hosts.block: Don't block the whole domain. Most iCloud services run under it, so iCloud sync, Private Relay and more stop.
breaks: iCloud Drive, iCloud Photos and app data in iCloud may stop syncing.
iCloud Private Relay and other iCloud features stop.
hosts.summary: Apple's iCloud domain. Apple lists *.icloud.com for iCloud services; specific hosts under it have their own pages.

hosts.block: Don't block it. iCloud services use it, so files, photos and attachments may stop syncing.
breaks: iCloud Drive, iCloud Photos and other iCloud content may stop uploading and downloading.
iMessage photos and other attachments may fail to send or arrive.
hosts.summary: An Apple domain for iCloud services. Large uploads and downloads of iCloud content, such as files and photos, can go to hosts under it.

hosts.block: Don't block them. Signing in to your Apple Account fails, and with it iCloud, the App Store and Xcode sign-in.
breaks: Signing in to iCloud, the App Store, Xcode and other Apple services fails.
Two-factor checks and password confirmations may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's Apple Account authentication hosts. Signing in to iCloud, the App Store and Xcode needs them.

hosts.block: Blocking it stops App Store downloads and updates, and other store content. Turn off automatic updates instead.
breaks: App Store apps can't install or update.
Books, music and other store content may not download.
hosts.summary: Apple's store content host, for apps, books and music.

hosts.block: Safe to block if your network has no Content Caching Mac. Devices then download Apple content directly.
breaks: Devices can't find a Content Caching Mac, so they download updates and apps from the internet instead.
hosts.summary: Apple's Content Caching locator, which devices ask to find a caching Mac on their network.

hosts.block: Safe to block if this Mac doesn't offer Content Caching. If it does, caching stops working.
breaks: This Mac can't register as a Content Caching server, so other devices download from Apple directly.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts that a Content Caching Mac uses to register, get its configuration and report.

hosts.block: Blocking it can stop iCloud Private Relay from working. Apple doesn't document its exact role.
breaks: iCloud Private Relay may fail to set up or connect.
hosts.summary: An iCloud Private Relay host on TCP 443. Unlike the relay hosts, Apple says that it supports proxies.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops iCloud Private Relay on that network. Turning off Limit IP address tracking for that network does the same thing cleanly.
breaks: iCloud Private Relay can't connect, so it stops hiding your IP address from websites on that network.
Browsing and DNS lookups then go out directly, without the relay's protection.
hosts.summary: The iCloud Private Relay hosts. With Private Relay on, Safari browsing and DNS lookups go through them.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Devices can't read Apple's software update catalogs, so they may not find updates.
breaks: Software Update may not find available updates.
Security responses and other update content listed in the catalogs may not install.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for software update catalogs, the lists of updates that devices check against.

hosts.block: Blocking it stops iCloud device diagnostics from reaching Apple. Apple doesn't document whether iCloud services depend on it.
breaks: iCloud device diagnostics can't reach Apple. Apple doesn't document other effects.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for iCloud device diagnostics.

hosts.block: Blocking it breaks some App Store content. Apps you already have keep working.
breaks: Store content hosted there, such as apps, books and music, may not download.
hosts.summary: An Apple domain for store content such as apps, books and music, and apps from websites and alternative marketplaces.

hosts.block: Don't block it. The Mac can't check whether Apple-issued certificates were revoked, and Apple services can fail.
breaks: Certificate checks for Apple's services may fail, so those services can stop connecting.
Revoked Apple-issued certificates may not be detected.
hosts.summary: Apple's certificate status (OCSP) servers. The Mac asks them whether an Apple-issued certificate has been revoked.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops OneDrive sync. To save data, pause OneDrive or cap its rate instead.
breaks: The OneDrive app can't upload or download files.
onedrive.live.com doesn't load in the browser.
hosts.summary: Hosts that Microsoft lists for consumer OneDrive, for file storage and the OneDrive service.

hosts.block: Blocking them doesn't affect normal use, but reinstalling macOS over the internet from Recovery fails.
breaks: Reinstalling macOS from macOS Recovery over the internet fails.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for macOS Recovery, used when you reinstall macOS over the internet.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops Apple Intelligence requests that need Private Cloud Compute. On-device features keep working.
breaks: Apple Intelligence features that use Private Cloud Compute fail.
hosts.summary: Hosts on Cloudflare and Fastly that Apple lists for Private Cloud Compute, where some Apple Intelligence requests are processed.

hosts.block: Blocking them may affect how Apple devices test their iCloud connection. Apple doesn't say what else depends on them.
breaks: iCloud connection tests fail. Apple doesn't document the effect on iCloud services.
hosts.summary: Apple's iCloud connection testing hosts.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime calls and many iCloud updates arrive through it.
breaks: App notifications stop arriving.
iMessage, FaceTime and phone calls on the Mac can't receive.
iCloud services that wait for a push, such as mail and calendars, update late.
hosts.summary: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs). The Mac keeps one connection to it, so notifications, iMessage, FaceTime calls and iCloud changes can arrive.

hosts.block: Blocking it stops npm and npx from installing public packages, unless you use another registry.
breaks: npm install and npx can't download public packages.
AI agents and tools that install npm packages fail.
hosts.summary: The npm public registry, where npm downloads JavaScript packages by default.

hosts.block: Safe to block if you don't want web suggestions. Local search keeps working. Turning suggestions off in settings is cleaner.
breaks: Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions from the web stop.
Look Up and search in News, Messages and Music may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's search services, for suggestions in Siri, Spotlight, Look Up, Safari, News, Messages and Music.

hosts.block: Blocking it stops macOS updates from downloading. Turn off automatic downloads instead, then update on your usual network.
breaks: macOS updates can't download, so security fixes wait.
Other update content that Apple hosts there may not download.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for macOS update downloads. Big transfers from it are macOS updates.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Apple lists it as needed for macOS updates.
breaks: Software Update may fail to check for or install macOS updates.
hosts.summary: An Apple host for macOS updates, listed in Apple's software update section.

hosts.block: Blocking it can stop macOS updates downloading. Turn off automatic downloads instead, then update on your usual network.
breaks: macOS update downloads may fail, so security fixes wait.
hosts.summary: An Apple host for macOS update downloads. Apple says that it works through proxies.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Apple lists it as needed for macOS updates.
breaks: Software Update may fail to check for or install macOS updates.
hosts.summary: An Apple host for macOS updates, listed in Apple's software update section.

hosts.block: Safe to block. Aerial screen savers and wallpapers that aren't downloaded yet won't download. Pick a still wallpaper to avoid the downloads.
breaks: Aerial screen savers and wallpapers that aren't on the Mac yet can't download.
hosts.summary: Apple's host for Aerial screen savers and wallpapers on tvOS and macOS.

hosts.block: Don't block them unless the Mac uses another time server. A clock that drifts makes secure websites fail with certificate errors.
breaks: The Mac's clock drifts. Secure sites can then show certificate errors, such as ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID.
Sign-ins and other features that check the time may fail.
hosts.summary: Apple's time servers. Macs use NTP on UDP port 123 to set their date and time from them.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Safari may stop warning you about fraudulent websites.
breaks: Safari's fraudulent website warnings may stop working, so phishing sites aren't flagged.
hosts.summary: The Apple host for Safari's fraudulent website warnings.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops software update downloads. Turn off automatic downloads instead, then update on your usual network.
breaks: Software update downloads fail, so security fixes wait.
Other Apple update content hosted there may not download.
hosts.summary: Apple's hosts for software update downloads, over HTTPS and plain HTTP, for all Apple platforms.

hosts.block: Don't block it. Apple lists it as needed to validate certificates, so secure connections to Apple can fail.
breaks: Certificate validation for Apple's services may fail, so those services can stop connecting.
hosts.summary: An Apple certificate validation host. Apple lists it for every platform, on port 443, with proxy support.

hosts.block: Apple doesn't say what it does, only that devices need it for software updates. Blocking it may affect updates.
breaks: Not documented. Because Apple lists it for software updates, updates may fail or report incomplete status.
hosts.summary: An Apple host that Apple lists in the software update section of its host list, without saying what it does.

hosts.block: Blocking them stops Zoom meetings, sign-in and updates. To save data, turn off video in meetings instead.
breaks: The Zoom app can't sign in or join meetings.
Zoom's website doesn't load.
hosts.summary: Zoom's domains for all Zoom clients, over TCP 80 and 443 and UDP 443.

processes.block: Blocking it saves almost no data and may keep your ad privacy choices from reaching Apple. Use the Apple Advertising setting instead.
breaks: Changes to Personalized Ads may not take effect on Apple's side.
Apple doesn't document its other tasks, so ad-related features in the App Store and News may behave differently.
processes.name: adprivacyd
processes.normal: Small, occasional connections are usual. It runs about every three days and after account changes.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security › Apple Advertising.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It manages advertising privacy for Apple's own ads in the App Store, Apple News and Stocks, including your opt-out from personalized ads.

processes.block: Blocking it doesn't save internet data. AirPlay from this Mac to TVs and speakers may stop working.
breaks: Streaming video or audio from this Mac to an Apple TV, a smart TV or an AirPlay speaker may fail.
Screen mirroring to a TV may fail.
Apple doesn't document the helper's other services, so other AirPlay features may be affected too.
processes.name: AirPlayXPCHelper
processes.normal: Traffic while you stream to a TV or a speaker is expected. Video takes much more than audio.
processes.reduce: Stop streaming when you don't need it. Click the AirPlay button in the app, then deselect the TV or speaker.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, not documented by Apple. Its name and its launchd services point to AirPlay, the streaming of video and audio between Apple devices and TVs.

processes.block: Don't block or stop them. They run Wi-Fi itself, so blocking them saves no data and can break joining networks.
breaks: The Mac may fail to join or stay on Wi-Fi networks.
Wi-Fi password prompts and other Wi-Fi tasks in your session may not appear.
processes.name: airportd
processes.normal: Little or no internet traffic of their own is normal. Activity Monitor counts the apps' traffic, not Wi-Fi management.
processes.reduce: There is nothing to reduce. Their work is the Wi-Fi connection itself.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. airportd manages the Wi-Fi interface, and WiFiAgent does Wi-Fi tasks for it in your session. They run Wi-Fi itself, not internet traffic.

processes.block: Don't block it. Signing in to your Apple Account, and every service that needs it, can fail.
breaks: Signing in to iCloud, the App Store and other Apple services can fail.
Sign in with Apple in apps and on websites can fail.
Two-factor codes and account checks may not complete.
processes.name: akd
processes.normal: Short, small connections are usual, after sign-in and from time to time in the background.
processes.reduce: There is no setting to reduce it. Its traffic is the minimum that your Apple Account needs.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, not documented by Apple. It is the AuthKit daemon, and its launchd services cover Apple Account sign-in and Sign in with Apple.

processes.block: Safe to block. Apple just stops getting your analytics. Turning off Share Mac Analytics does the same thing cleanly.
breaks: Apple stops getting your diagnostic and usage data.
Nothing that you use on the Mac depends on sending analytics.
processes.name: analyticsd
processes.normal: Little network traffic is usual. Most of its work is local.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security. Click Analytics & Improvements.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It collects diagnostics and usage data on the Mac for users who opted in to sharing analytics.

processes.block: Blocking them stops App Store downloads and updates. Apps you have keep working. On a hotspot, turn off automatic updates instead.
breaks: App Store apps can't install, download again or update.
Security fixes in App Store apps stop arriving.
Apps you buy or download again from the App Store can't arrive on this Mac.
processes.name: appstoreagent
processes.normal: Bursts of traffic when apps update are usual. Large apps, such as Xcode or games, can be several gigabytes.
processes.reduce: Open the App Store. Choose App Store › Settings.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. They download and update apps from the App Store, so app downloads show under them, not under the App Store app.

processes.block: Don't block it. Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime calls and iCloud updates all arrive through it.
breaks: Notifications from apps stop arriving.
iMessage and FaceTime can't receive messages or calls, and phone calls on the Mac stop ringing.
iCloud services that wait for a push, such as new mail or calendar changes, update late or not at all.
processes.name: apsd
processes.normal: A steady, small connection is how push notifications work. Its traffic is usually small.
processes.reduce: Turn off notifications for apps that you don't need. Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Notifications.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It keeps one connection open to Apple's push notification service, so apps and iCloud can tell the Mac that something changed.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't need it, but it's better to turn Content Caching off in Sharing settings. Other devices then download from Apple directly.
breaks: Other Apple devices on the network download updates and apps from Apple instead of from this Mac.
On a capped connection, each device then uses its own internet data for the same update.
heavy: An iOS or macOS release day
processes.name: AssetCache
processes.normal: If you turned on Content Caching, large uploads on the local network are its purpose. They don't use your internet connection.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is Content Caching. It keeps Apple downloads on this Mac and gives them to other Apple devices on the same network.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't use Siri, but Siri and server dictation stop. It's cleaner to turn Siri off in System Settings.
breaks: Siri can't answer requests that need Apple's servers.
Dictation that uses Apple's servers stops.
Apple doesn't document which Siri features work offline.
processes.name: assistantd
processes.normal: When you use Siri, small requests are usual. Apple doesn't publish how much data Siri uses.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Siri. In older versions, the name is Siri & Spotlight.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the Siri daemon, so Siri requests and dictation that need Apple's servers can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking it stops iCloud Drive sync on this Mac. Your files stay here, but changes stop reaching your other devices.
breaks: Files you add or change in iCloud Drive don't upload, and changes from your other devices don't arrive.
Files kept only in iCloud can't download to this Mac until you allow it again.
With Desktop & Documents Folders on, those folders stop syncing too.
heavy: You turn on Desktop & Documents Folders
Big files in a synced folder
processes.name: bird
processes.normal: Traffic after you add or change files is usual. The amount is the size of the files, plus a little overhead.
processes.reduce: Do large copies into iCloud Drive on your usual network, not on a hotspot.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs iCloud Drive, so its traffic is your iCloud Drive files going up and down.

processes.block: Blocking them stops phone calls on this Mac. Your iPhone still rings. Turn off calls on the Mac instead.
breaks: The Mac can't make or receive phone calls through your iPhone.
Call notifications on the Mac stop.
FaceTime call state on the Mac may be affected. Apple doesn't document every use of the call server.
processes.name: callservicesd
processes.normal: Without calls, their traffic is small or none.
processes.reduce: On your iPhone, open Settings › Apps › Phone › Calls on Other Devices. Turn off this Mac.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. callservicesd keeps the state of calls, and CommCenter lets the Mac make and receive phone calls through your iPhone.

processes.block: Don't block it. Chrome can't load pages without its helpers. Block the website instead.
breaks: Chrome can't load pages, because its tabs and network service run in helpers.
Extensions stop working.
A rule on the helper acts on all browsing in Chrome. Block the host instead, for every app or only Chrome.
processes.name: Google Chrome Helper
processes.normal: A lot of traffic while you browse is normal. It is the sites you visit.
paths: /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/Frameworks/Google Chrome Framework.framework/Helpers/Google Chrome Helper.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome Helper
processes.reduce: Close tabs that play video or refresh in the background.
processes.summary: Part of Google Chrome. Chrome runs its tabs, extensions and network service in helper processes, so your browsing shows under Google Chrome Helper.

processes.block: Don't block it. iCloud sync for many apps stops, and Apple says that macOS security data also comes through CloudKit.
breaks: Apps that keep data in iCloud stop syncing with your other devices. Changes stay on this Mac until you allow it again.
Shared notes, reminders and other shared iCloud data stop updating.
CloudKit content that macOS needs, such as XProtect updates, can't download.
heavy: A new Mac or a new sign-in
An app with a lot of data in iCloud
You turn on iCloud for an app
processes.name: cloudd
processes.normal: Short bursts after you change something in an app are usual. The size depends on what changed.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then click iCloud.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It syncs the iCloud data of apps that use CloudKit, so its traffic belongs to those apps.

processes.block: Blocking it stops iCloud Photos sync on this Mac. Photos already here stay. Use Photos' Pause button instead to stop uploads for a day.
breaks: New photos and videos on this Mac don't upload, and photos from your other devices don't arrive.
With Optimize Storage, originals that are only in iCloud can't download.
Shared Library changes stop syncing.
processes.name: cloudphotod
processes.normal: A large upload after an import is usual. Apple says that a big library can need to sync overnight, and that some larger files take longer.
processes.reduce: To pause uploads for one day, open Photos. Click Library, then All Photos.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It does all iCloud Photos sync, so its traffic is your photos and videos going up and down.

processes.block: Don't block it. Without DHCP, the Mac can't get an address on most networks, and then nothing connects.
breaks: The Mac can't get or renew its IP address on networks that use DHCP.
IPv6 configuration from router advertisements and DHCPv6 stops.
Network changes, such as joining a new Wi-Fi network, may not apply.
processes.name: configd
processes.normal: DHCP and router messages are tiny, a few packets at a time.
processes.reduce: There is nothing to reduce. Its traffic is the minimum that a network connection needs.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It keeps the Mac's network configuration and gets its IP addresses with DHCP, so it sends small amounts of traffic to the router.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Dropbox sync on this Mac. Your files stay, but changes don't reach other devices. Pause sync instead.
breaks: Files don't upload or download, so this Mac and your other devices drift apart.
Shared folders stop updating for you.
Updates to the Dropbox app can't download, and LAN sync stops.
processes.name: Dropbox
processes.normal: Bursts after you change files are usual. The amount is about the size of the files.
processes.reduce: To pause, click the Dropbox icon in the menu bar. Click the sync status at the bottom of the window.
processes.summary: The Dropbox desktop app. It uploads and downloads your Dropbox files, and with LAN sync it finds other Dropbox computers on the local network.

processes.block: Blocking a helper breaks the app it belongs to. Block or pause the app itself, or block the host it shouldn't reach.
breaks: The app's windows may stop loading or updating.
Its sign-in, sync and calls may fail.
Its updates can't download.

processes.name: Electron Helper
processes.normal: The traffic is whatever the app does. A chat app is light until someone shares a video; a call app is heavy during calls.
processes.reduce: Find the app's name in the helper's name. Open that app's settings.
processes.summary: Part of an app built on Electron. Electron apps run their windows and their network work in helper processes, so the app's traffic shows under “App Helper”.

processes.block: Don't block it. The Finder needs it to show cloud files, and every File Provider app depends on it. Pause the cloud app instead.
breaks: Cloud files in the Finder may fail to open, list or sync, for iCloud Drive and other providers.
Saving into a cloud folder may fail.
processes.name: fileproviderd
processes.normal: When a cloud storage app syncs, traffic is usual. Each provider app also moves data in its own processes. Look at both.
processes.reduce: Pause sync in the cloud storage app. Use the app's menu bar item or its settings.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It connects cloud storage apps built on File Provider to the Finder, so their file downloads and uploads can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking them can stop Find My from locating this Mac. Keep Find My on if you want to find a lost or stolen Mac.
breaks: Find My may not show this Mac's location, so a lost or stolen Mac is harder to find.
This Mac may stop helping to find other people's missing devices.
Apple doesn't document all of searchpartyd's work, so other Find My features may be affected.
processes.name: findmydeviced
processes.normal: With Find My Mac on, the traffic is small.
processes.reduce: Keep Find My Mac on. It helps you find a lost or stolen Mac.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. findmydeviced runs Find My Mac. searchpartyd is another Find My daemon that Apple doesn't describe in its man page.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Chrome and other Google app updates, including security fixes. On a hotspot, pause it and update later instead.
breaks: Chrome and other Google apps stop updating, and security fixes don't arrive.
Chrome's About page can't update the browser.
heavy: A server that asks to retry
processes.name: GoogleUpdater
processes.normal: Small checks every few hours are usual when you have Google apps.
processes.reduce: Keep Chrome up to date. Updates fix security problems.
processes.summary: Google's updater for Chrome and other Google apps on the Mac. It checks for updates about every few hours and downloads new versions.

processes.block: Don't block it. iMessage, FaceTime and features between your own devices need it to find keys and devices.
breaks: iMessage can't send to new contacts, and FaceTime calls may fail to connect.
Features between your own devices that rely on IDS may stop.
Screen Time data from a child's devices may not reach a parent.
processes.name: identityservicesd
processes.normal: When you use Messages or FaceTime, small lookups are usual.
processes.reduce: If you don't use iMessage on this Mac, open Messages. Choose Messages › Settings › iMessage and sign out.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the client of the Apple Identity Service, which finds the keys and devices of the people you message or call.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Messages on this Mac. Your iPhone keeps working. Sign out of iMessage on the Mac if you don't use it here.
breaks: Messages on this Mac can't send or receive iMessages.
Attachments can't upload or download.
Apple doesn't document what else depends on it, so other Messages features may fail too.
processes.name: imagent
processes.normal: Text messages are small. Photos and videos are the large part.
processes.reduce: If you don't use Messages on this Mac, open Messages. Choose Messages › Settings › iMessage and sign out.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, not documented by Apple. It is the agent behind the Messages app, in the IMCore framework, so iMessage traffic can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking it can stop apps and features from getting your location. To control it, use Location Services in Privacy & Security.
breaks: Apps that you allowed may not get your location, or get it less accurately.
Find My Mac may not show where the Mac is.
System services listed under Location Services › System Services may lose your location.
processes.name: locationd
processes.normal: When apps with permission ask for your location, small traffic is usual.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs Location Services, finding where the Mac is for the apps you allowed.

processes.block: Don't block it. Every app on the Mac uses it to look up names, so blocking it breaks almost all connections.
breaks: Apps can't look up names, so websites and most internet connections fail.
Bonjour stops, so AirPlay, AirPrint and shared computers can't be found.
A firewall rule for it acts on every app's DNS lookups, not one app. Block the app, or the host, instead.
heavy: An app that looks up many names
processes.name: mDNSResponder
processes.normal: DNS answers are small, so mDNSResponder usually moves less data than the apps that it works for.
processes.reduce: Find the app that makes the lookups. Its own traffic often rises at the same time in Activity Monitor.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It does the DNS lookups of every app and runs Bonjour on the local network, so its traffic is other apps' name lookups.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Office and other Microsoft app updates, including security fixes. On a hotspot, pause it or update later instead.
breaks: Office, Teams and other Microsoft apps stop getting updates and security fixes.
Help › Check for Updates in Microsoft apps can't find updates.
heavy: A Mac that was off for a while
processes.name: Microsoft AutoUpdate
processes.normal: Small checks a couple of times a day are usual.
processes.reduce: Open a Microsoft app, such as Word. Choose Help › Check for Updates. The MAU window opens.
processes.summary: Microsoft's updater for Office, Teams and other Microsoft apps on the Mac. It checks for updates and, by default, downloads and installs them.

processes.block: Blocking it stops downloads of models, voices and other assets that macOS features need. To stop the biggest download, turn off Apple Intelligence.
breaks: Apple Intelligence can't finish setting up, and new models after an update don't arrive.
New voices, languages and dictionaries can't download.
Apple doesn't document every asset it handles, so other features that need a download may fail too.
processes.name: mobileassetd
processes.normal: Downloads after a macOS update, or after you turn on a feature, are usual. Apple Intelligence models can be several gigabytes.
processes.reduce: Do macOS updates on your usual network. The asset downloads follow them.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, not documented by Apple. Kilobat sees it download system assets such as Apple Intelligence models, voices, fonts and dictionaries.

processes.block: Don't block them. VPNs and content filters, including Kilobat's firewall, can't run without them.
breaks: VPN connections can't start, or stop carrying traffic.
Content filters, including Kilobat's network filter, stop working.
VPN and filter settings may fail to apply.
processes.name: nesessionmanager
processes.normal: With a VPN on, a lot of traffic under these processes is normal. It is your traffic, inside the tunnel.
processes.reduce: To stop a VPN, turn it off in the VPN app or in Apple menu › System Settings › VPN.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. They run Network Extension sessions, such as VPNs and content filters, and host their plug-ins, so VPN traffic can show under them.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't share files with Windows computers. It's cleaner to turn off File Sharing, which configures it.
breaks: Windows computers may not find this Mac by its NetBIOS name.
Browsing Windows computers and workgroups from the Finder may show fewer computers.
processes.name: netbiosd
processes.normal: Small local traffic is usual. It doesn't use your internet connection.
processes.reduce: Check whether you share files. Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It registers and browses NetBIOS names for Windows-style file sharing. Its traffic stays on the local network.

processes.block: Blocking it can break iCloud Private Relay and Apple services that use its proxy. To stop the relay, turn off Private Relay instead.
breaks: iCloud Private Relay can't connect, so Safari may fail to load pages while it is on.
Apple system services that use the proxy may fail. Apple doesn't list them.
processes.name: networkserviceproxy
processes.normal: With Private Relay off, its traffic is usually small.
processes.reduce: To turn off Private Relay, choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then iCloud, then Private Relay.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the transparent proxy for Apple system services and can carry iCloud Private Relay traffic, so other apps' browsing can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking node blocks every Node.js program at once. Block the specific host instead, or stop the script you don't recognise.
breaks: npm and npx can't install packages.
Dev servers, CLIs, AI agents and MCP servers that run on Node.js lose the network.
The rule applies to every program that this node binary runs.
processes.maker: OpenJS Foundation (Node.js), installed by you or a tool
processes.name: node
processes.normal: Traffic while you install packages or run a tool is normal.
processes.reduce: Find what the process runs. In Terminal, show its command line, using its process ID.
processes.summary: The Node.js runtime, not part of macOS. It connects only when a script asks, such as npm installing packages, a dev server, an AI agent or an MCP server.

processes.block: Blocking it stops the background downloads and uploads of every app that hands transfers to macOS. Pause the one app instead.
breaks: Background downloads in apps that use it, such as podcast episodes and media for offline use, wait or fail.
Background uploads from those apps wait or fail.
Each app decides what to show when the transfer fails, so the error may not name the network.
processes.name: nsurlsessiond
processes.normal: Some nsurlsessiond traffic is a normal part of macOS. The amount depends only on what your apps asked for. With no pending transfers, it is quiet.
processes.reduce: Find the app that asked for the download. Think about what you started just before, for example a podcast subscription.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It does background downloads and uploads that apps hand to macOS, so its traffic belongs to those apps.

processes.block: Blocking it stops OneDrive sync on this Mac. Your local files stay, but changes don't reach the cloud. Pause it or cap its rate instead.
breaks: Files don't upload or download, so this Mac and your other devices drift apart.
Office files saved to OneDrive don't reach your other devices.
Sign-in to OneDrive may fail if its sign-in hosts are blocked too.
processes.name: OneDrive
processes.normal: Bursts after you change files are usual. The amount is about the size of the files.
processes.reduce: Control-click the OneDrive icon in the menu bar. Choose to pause for 2, 8 or 24 hours. Microsoft says that sync resumes on its own after that.
processes.summary: Microsoft's OneDrive sync app. It uploads and downloads your OneDrive files. Microsoft says that it pauses on metered networks on its own.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't want web suggestions. Local Spotlight search keeps working. It's cleaner to turn suggestions off in settings.
breaks: Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions from the web stop appearing.
Look Up and
Apple News article search may stop working.
processes.name: parsecd
processes.normal: Small requests while you search are usual.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Spotlight. Turn off the search results and suggestions that you don't use.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It handles Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions and Look Up, so it connects to Apple while you search or type.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Apple Intelligence features that need Private Cloud Compute. On-device features keep working.
breaks: Apple Intelligence requests that need a larger model fail.
Features that use Private Cloud Compute, as listed in the Apple Intelligence Report, stop working.
processes.name: privatecloudcomputed
processes.normal: When you use Apple Intelligence, some traffic is expected. Each request and answer is small next to a download.
processes.reduce: Use fewer Apple Intelligence features, or turn Apple Intelligence off in System Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It encrypts and sends Apple Intelligence requests that need a larger model to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers.

processes.block: Blocking it is safe for the internet, but Handoff and other features between your Apple devices stop.
breaks: Handoff between this Mac and your other devices stops.
Phone call handoff and other Continuity features that need it may stop.
Blocking incoming connections for it in the macOS firewall has the same effect on the features that listen.
processes.name: rapportd
processes.normal: Small amounts of local traffic are usual when you have other Apple devices nearby.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › AirDrop & Continuity.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It connects this Mac to your other Apple devices on the local network for Handoff, phone calls and other Continuity features.

processes.block: Blocking them doesn't save internet data. Xcode's wireless installs and debugging, and other paired-device features, stop.
breaks: Xcode can't find, install to or debug a device over the network.
Other features that discover paired devices may stop. Apple doesn't document them all.
heavy: Installing a build on a device
processes.name: remotepairingd
processes.normal: If you use Xcode with a device, or another feature that pairs devices, traffic to that device is expected.
processes.reduce: Connect the device with a cable when you install or debug apps.
processes.summary: Part of macOS and Xcode's device support. They find and talk to paired iPhones and iPads, mostly on the local network.

processes.block: Safe to block. Nothing you use depends on it. It's cleaner to turn off Share Mac Analytics, which stops the uploads.
breaks: Apple stops getting your diagnostic reports, which help it fix bugs.
Developers who receive reports through Apple, with Share with app developers on, stop getting yours.
processes.name: SubmitDiagInfo
processes.normal: If you share analytics, the uploads are small and periodic.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security. Click Analytics & Improvements.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. ReportCrash saves crash reports on the Mac. SubmitDiagInfo sends diagnostic and usage information to Apple, but only if you opted in.

processes.block: Safe to block if nobody needs to reach this Mac remotely. It's better to turn off Screen Sharing in Sharing settings.
breaks: Other computers can't view or control this Mac with Screen Sharing or a VNC app.
Apple Remote Desktop management of this Mac stops, if your organization uses it.
processes.name: screensharingd
processes.normal: With no session open, its traffic is small or none.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It accepts Screen Sharing and VNC connections from other computers, so another person can see and control this Mac.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Screen Time data syncing between devices. For a child's device, it can stop limits from arriving.
breaks: Screen Time reports stop including your other devices.
Changes a parent makes to a child's limits may not arrive, and the child's usage may not reach the parent.
processes.name: ScreenTimeAgent
processes.normal: Small, occasional sync traffic is usual with Screen Time on.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Screen Time.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It supports Screen Time, which can sync your usage and limits across your devices through iCloud.

processes.block: Don't block it. Apps that use the keychain depend on it, and iCloud Keychain sync stops.
breaks: Passwords, passkeys and Wi-Fi passwords stop syncing with your other devices.
New devices can't join your iCloud Keychain.
Apps on this Mac that read the keychain may fail if keychain access is affected.
processes.name: secd
processes.normal: Small, occasional sync traffic is usual with iCloud Keychain on. Keychain items are small.
processes.reduce: To stop syncing passwords on this Mac, choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then iCloud.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It controls access to keychain items. With iCloud Keychain on, your passwords and other synced items travel between your devices.

processes.block: Blocking it is safe for your internet data, but AirDrop, Handoff and Instant Hotspot discovery may stop working.
breaks: AirDrop can't find devices or send files.
Handoff and Instant Hotspot discovery may stop.
Shared computers in the Finder sidebar may not appear.
processes.name: sharingd
processes.normal: Traffic during an AirDrop transfer is usual. It is about as large as the files you send or receive.
processes.reduce: Open Control Center and click AirDrop. Choose Contacts Only, or turn AirDrop off.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs AirDrop, Handoff, Instant Hotspot discovery and the shared computers in the Finder. AirDrop transfers can show under it.

processes.block: Safe to block for a while, but the app then can't install its updates. Block or pause the app's download instead.
breaks: Downloaded updates of the app can't be installed.
The app may try again each time it starts.
processes.maker: Squirrel.Mac, bundled by each Electron app
processes.name: ShipIt
processes.normal: ShipIt runs for a short time when an app updates. Its own traffic is small or none.
processes.reduce: Open the settings of the app. Turn off automatic updates, if the app has that option.
processes.summary: Part of Squirrel.Mac, the updater that many Electron apps include. It installs an update that the app has already downloaded.

processes.block: Blocking it stops shortcuts syncing between devices and can break shortcuts that use the internet.
breaks: Shortcuts don't sync with your other devices.
Shortcuts with web actions can fail when they run.
Updated malware definitions for shortcuts may not arrive.
processes.name: siriactionsd
processes.normal: Sync traffic is small. Shortcuts are small files.
processes.reduce: Look at the shortcuts that run on a schedule. Open Shortcuts and click Automations.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs and syncs the shortcuts you make in the Shortcuts app, so iCloud sync of shortcuts can show under it.

processes.block: Safe to block if no other computer needs this Mac's files. It's cleaner to turn off File Sharing in Sharing settings.
breaks: Other Macs and PCs can't open this Mac's shared folders.
Backups that other computers make to a shared folder here stop.
heavy: An app working on shared files
processes.name: smbd
processes.normal: With nobody connected, it is quiet.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the SMB file server for File Sharing, so its traffic is other computers reading and writing this Mac's shared folders.

processes.block: Don't block it for long. The Mac stops getting macOS and security updates. On a hotspot, turn off automatic downloads instead.
breaks: macOS updates and upgrades can't download or install. Apple's server must sign each update.
Security responses and system data files stop arriving, so security fixes fall behind.
Software Update in System Settings and the softwareupdate command can't check for updates.
processes.name: softwareupdated
processes.normal: Checks are small and short. Large downloads after Apple releases an update are expected.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Software Update. Click the Info button next to Automatic Updates.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It checks for and downloads macOS updates, security responses and system files.

processes.block: Safe to block for a while. The app keeps working, but it stops updating. Turn off automatic downloads in the app instead.
breaks: The app can't install its updates, so security fixes wait.
Each app's check for updates fails while it's blocked.
processes.maker: Sparkle project, bundled by each app
processes.name: Autoupdate
processes.normal: Each app that uses Sparkle checks once a day by default. The checks are small.
processes.reduce: Open the app's settings. Many apps that use Sparkle have options to check for and download updates automatically.
processes.summary: Part of Sparkle, an open-source update framework that many Mac apps include. It installs an update after the app downloads it.

processes.block: Safe to block if nobody logs in to this Mac remotely. It's cleaner to turn off Remote Login in Sharing settings.
breaks: SSH, SFTP and scp to this Mac stop working.
Tools that connect to this Mac over SSH, such as remote editors and deploy scripts, fail.
processes.name: sshd
processes.normal: With Remote Login off, nothing listens on port 22.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the SSH server for Remote Login, so other computers can log in to this Mac with SSH or copy files with SFTP.

processes.block: Apple doesn't document what its connections are for. Blocking them may affect suggestions; the settings below turn the features off instead.
breaks: Not documented. Suggestions in Mail, Messages, the keyboard and Siri may get worse or stop.
Found in Apps contacts and events may not appear.
processes.name: suggestd
processes.normal: The man page describes its work as processing content, so CPU use is more likely than network traffic.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Siri. Find the suggestion settings for each app.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It reads content from Mail, Messages and other apps on the Mac to suggest contacts and events. Apple doesn't document much network use.

processes.block: Apple doesn't document what depends on it. Blocking it saves little data and may affect features that Apple doesn't name.
breaks: Not documented. Apple doesn't say which features use the Symptom Framework.
Because it runs as the networking user and reacts to network changes, network features may be affected.
processes.name: symptomsd
processes.normal: It is part of macOS and usually shows little or no traffic of its own.
processes.reduce: There is no user setting for symptomsd.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, barely documented. Apple says only that it provides services for the Symptom Framework. It runs as the networking user and reacts to network changes.

processes.block: Don't block it. Gatekeeper's online checks protect the Mac against known malware and revoked apps.
breaks: Gatekeeper can't check new apps online for known malware or revoked developer certificates.
Revocation tickets for malicious apps may not reach this Mac.
Opening a new app can take longer while the check waits for the network.
processes.name: syspolicyd
processes.normal: Short connections when you open new or updated apps are usual. They are small.
processes.reduce: There is no setting to reduce these checks safely. They are small.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs the system policy that includes Gatekeeper, which checks new and changed apps for known malware and revoked certificates.

processes.block: Don't block it. A wrong clock makes valid certificates look expired, so secure websites and apps fail.
breaks: The clock drifts. Secure websites can then show certificate errors, such as ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID.
Sign-ins and other features that check the time may fail.
Apple doesn't list a fallback for macOS without NTP.
processes.name: timed
processes.normal: The requests are tiny. A time request and its answer are a few small packets.
processes.reduce: There is nothing to reduce. Keep it on. See “This Connection Is Not Private” and certificate warnings on a Mac.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It keeps the clock correct with NTP, so it sends small requests to a time server such as time.apple.com.

processes.block: Don't block it. macOS then can't check whether certificates were revoked, and Apple services that need validation can fail.
breaks: macOS can't tell whether a certificate was revoked, which weakens every secure connection.
Apple says that its devices must reach the certificate validation hosts to validate the certificates of its own services.
On a company network, a proxy that blocks these checks causes certificate errors. See Corporate proxy certificates break Terminal tools on a Mac.
heavy: A first visit to many sites
processes.name: trustd
processes.normal: Small, short connections are usual, mostly when you visit many secure sites or open apps.
processes.reduce: There is no user setting for these checks. They protect every secure connection.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It checks certificates for every app, and asks certificate authorities whether a certificate was revoked. Its connections are small.

processes.block: Don't block it. Safari and every app that shows web pages stop loading. Block the website instead.
breaks: Safari can't load any page.
Apps that show web content through WebKit, such as Mail's remote content, stop loading it.
A rule on this process acts on all browsing. Block the host instead, for every app or one app.
processes.name: com.apple.WebKit.Networking
processes.normal: A lot of traffic is normal while you browse. It is the sites you visit.
processes.reduce: Close tabs that play video or refresh in the background.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is WebKit's network process, which does all network access for Safari and for apps that show web pages, so their browsing shows under it.

processes.block: You can't block it with a firewall, because it isn't internet traffic. To stop its link for a while, turn off AirDrop; Kilobat can pause it for you.
breaks: AirDrop can't find or send to nearby devices.
Other features that use the peer-to-peer link between nearby devices may stop.
processes.name: wifip2pd
processes.normal: wifip2pd itself moves little data. The bytes of a transfer belong to the feature that uses the link: AirDrop is under sharingd.
processes.reduce: Open Control Center and click AirDrop. Turn AirDrop off while you are on a call or playing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It manages peer-to-peer Wi-Fi, the direct link that AirDrop and other nearby-device features use.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Zoom meetings on this Mac. To save data, turn off video in meetings instead.
breaks: You can't join or host Zoom meetings in the desktop app.
Zoom Chat and other Zoom features in the app stop.
Updates to the app can't download.
processes.name: zoom.us
processes.normal: A lot of traffic during a meeting is normal. Video uses far more than audio.
processes.reduce: Turn off your camera when you don't need it. Video uses most of the data.
processes.summary: The Zoom desktop app. During meetings it sends and receives audio and video; Zoom also updates itself if automatic updates are on.
